subject: Art & Design
title: The Evolution of Special Effects
description: A quick, practical guide to The Evolution of Special Effects.

hook.text: In 1902, Georges Méliès made a rocket hit the Moon's eye using cardboard. A century later, Thanos felt real.

buildup.text: Special effects evolved from practical tricks — miniatures, matte paintings, stop-motion — to digital CGI worlds.

discovery.text: Jurassic Park (1993) was the turning point: animatronics plus CGI proved digital creatures could feel alive.

twist.text: More CGI doesn't mean better films. Mad Max: Fury Road (2015) used mostly practical stunts and won six Oscars.

climax.text: The Volume, LED walls used in The Mandalorian, merges practical and digital. Actors perform inside real-time CGI worlds.

punchline.text: The best effects are the ones you never notice.

quiz.question: What made Jurassic Park a turning point in special effects?
options: It proved digital CGI creatures could look convincingly real alongside practical effects
It was the first film to use any computer graphics
It eliminated the need for practical effects entirely

details.summary: Special effects evolved from Méliès' camera tricks through miniatures, matte paintings, and stop-motion to the CGI revolution that began with 'Jurassic Park' in 1993. Each era expanded what cinema could show, but the best effects serve story rather than replacing it.
details.whyItMatters: Effects technology determines cinema's visual boundaries. Understanding effects history shows how technical innovation enables new stories and why audiences sometimes prefer practical effects' tangible physicality over CGI's perfection.
takeaways: Effects evolved from camera tricks to matte paintings to CGI
Jurassic Park's 1993 CGI launched the digital revolution
The best effects always serve story over spectacle

faq.question: Why do some people prefer practical effects over CGI?
faq.answer: Practical effects — real explosions, prosthetic makeup, miniature models — have physical weight and imperfection that the brain recognizes as real. CGI can look too perfect or 'floaty.' Films like 'Mad Max: Fury Road' proved that practical effects still create more visceral impact than pure CGI.

faq.question: What was the first fully CGI character in a film?
faq.answer: The first photorealistic CGI character was the T-1000 in 'Terminator 2' (1991). 'Jurassic Park' (1993) created the first convincing CGI creatures. 'Toy Story' (1995) was the first entirely CGI feature film. Each pushed the technology forward by years.
